name: Lot
overview: Lot is a male figure in Scripture identified as the son of Haran and the nephew of Abram. His genealogy places him within the early patriarchal family, though no specific tribal affiliation is recorded. There are no additional notes on his unique attributes beyond these familial ties.
namesAndTitles: The name Lot, given in Genesis 11:27, means 'to cover' or 'enfold.' This proper name is not indicated as being given by God, but it reflects the Hebrew meaning associated with his identity.
familyAndRelationships: Lot is recorded as the son of Haran and the nephew of Abram. He is the husband of an unnamed wife and the father of two sons, referred to as his firstborn and younger son. Additionally, he is the father of Moab and Ben-ammi, who are significant as progenitors of peoples mentioned later in Scripture.
scriptureSignificance: Lot is significant as a relative of Abraham who journeyed with him to the land of Canaan. His choice to settle in the fertile plain near Sodom placed him amidst a corrupt environment, highlighting the peril of prioritizing worldly advantage over spiritual fidelity. His deliverance by angels from the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah illustrates God's mercy and foreshadows the salvation offered to believers. Furthermore, his characterization as a righteous man distressed by surrounding wickedness underscores the challenges of living faithfully in a fallen world.
